ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a triangle, with a vertical side on the left labeled 1.8; the slanted side from the upper-left vertex to the pointed vertex on the right is labeled 5.6; the slanted side from the lower-left vertex to the pointed vertex on the right is labeled 6.5. Angle x is located at the upper-left vertex, formed by the two sides of lengths 1.8 and 5.6, and the side of length 6.5 is opposite angle x. Reasoning: It is known that the two adjacent sides of angle x are 1.8 and 5.6, and the opposite side is 6.5, use the law of cosines: cos(x) = (1.8^2 + 5.6^2 - 6.5^2) / (2 × 1.8 × 5.6). Calculating gives 1.8^2 = 3.24, 5.6^2 = 31.36, 6.5^2 = 42.25, so cos(x) = (3.24 + 31.36 - 42.25) / 20.16 = -7.65 / 20.16 ≈ -0.3795. Thus x = arccos(-0.3795) ≈ 112.3°, rounded to the nearest integer degree is 112°.
